scenes.heading: Sharing electrons between atoms
scenes.narration: Atoms get close and start sharing electrons with each other, rather than giving them away completely, forming a strong link that holds the two particles tightly together.

scenes.heading: Achieving a stable outer shell
scenes.narration: Every single atom wants a full outer shell because that arrangement is remarkably unreactive and peaceful, so sharing lets them complete their outer shell without losing anything.

scenes.heading: Lower energy means greater stability
scenes.narration: The bonded state sits lower in energy than two separate atoms ever could, and because nature always prefers lower energy, this cozy arrangement provides lasting stability.

scenes.heading: Balancing forces in the bond
scenes.narration: Both positive nuclei pull strongly on the shared pair sitting between them, successfully balancing out the natural repulsion between the two positive centres so they stay put.

scenes.heading: Molecules like hydrogen and water
scenes.narration: Hydrogen gas molecules and water molecules both rely on this exact trick, using shared electrons to achieve full shells and low energy states all around us.
